admission.text: School/college review is selective. An Ontario average alone cannot establish admission; treat Michigan as a high reach.

acceptanceRate.text: No admission percentage is used in this planner.

sat.text: The current application permits optional SAT/ACT submission and self-reporting. Enrolling score submitters must provide official results. Fall2028 policy requires confirmation.

satMiddle50.text: SAT1370–1530: middle50% of Fall2025 enrolled first-year SAT submitters.55% submitted SAT; this is not an Ontario cutoff.

satTarget.text: Use the published range as score context only; even1500 cannot establish admission or compensate automatically for low school marks.

deadlines.text: Fall2028 deadlines are not yet verified. Current reference: binding ED and nonbinding EA November1; RD February1. Music/Theatre/Dance has a separate December1 deadline.

application.text: Common App, USD75, transcript, School Report, one academic recommendation and applicable English proof. Additional college portfolios/auditions may apply; confirm future essays.

ontario.text: At least five Grade12 U courses, including Grade12 U English, leading to OSSD are required. Apply during senior year. No Ontario percentage minimum is stated.

coursework.text: LSA expects English4 years, math/science/social studies3 each and world language2; four language years are encouraged. Confirm Ontario course equivalencies with Admissions.

international.text: Ontario schooling and citizenship are separate questions. Use the international curriculum instructions and confirm status-specific funding rules.

english.text: IELTS guidance:7.0 with sections6.5+. The stated waiver combines SAT reading/writing650+ (or ACT English and Reading27+) AND four recent rigorous years in listed countries including Canada except Quebec. Confirm individual eligibility.

majorStructure.text: LSA majors are normally declared in sophomore year. Sociology requires a qualifying introductory course at C− or better; History and Anthropology use departmental advising. These are post-enrollment rules, not freshman cutoffs.

recommendedMajors.text: Sociology, History and Anthropology are flexible LSA subjects to explore if they match your interests. No easier-entry advantage is established.

ap.text: High AP exam results may earn advanced standing under school-specific tables. AP enrollment alone does not earn credit; recheck the2028 table.

cost.text: 2026–27 LSA nonresident lower-division estimated annual budget: USD88,394, including tuition/fees67,096. This is a two-semester estimate, not a2028 international bill; program and individual costs vary.

aid.text: The admissions office says temporary-visa international students are ineligible for financial aid and should plan to pay full attendance costs. Confirm exceptional departmental awards and citizenship-based eligibility; no CSS-based grant is promised.

admission.text: Holistic review emphasizes strong academic preparation and achievement. UW explicitly does not use admission formulas or charts. No Ontario average cutoff was verified.

acceptanceRate.text: No defined-cohort admission percentage is used here.

sat.text: SAT/ACT are optional only through spring2028 in the published authorization. This does not establish the Fall2028 policy.

satMiddle50.text: A current official SAT cohort table could not be verified in this research; no range is invented.

satTarget.text: Confirm the Fall2028 test policy and a dated score distribution before setting a submission target.

deadlines.text: Fall2028 dates are not yet verified. Current fall reference: EA November1, materials November9; RD January15, materials January22. EA is nonbinding.

application.text: Common App or Universities of Wisconsin Application; USD80; two essays, courses/grades for Grades9–12, one academic recommendation and applicable English proof.

ontario.text: For an unlisted curriculum, send official Grades9–12-equivalent records and graduation credentials. No Ontario top-six formula or percentage minimum is verified; confirm U/M course equivalencies.

coursework.text: Minimums: English4 years; math, natural science and social science3 each; electives4. Math must include algebra, geometry and advanced math. Statistics alone does not satisfy the math requirement.

international.text: International students use the same first-year application, with curriculum-specific records. Funding eligibility depends on citizenship/visa status.

english.text: For applicants educated in non-English-speaking countries: English-medium study for all four secondary years may waive testing. Otherwise IELTS6.5+, DET115+, or TOEFL4.5 for tests from January21,2026 (80 for earlier tests). SAT/AP do not waive it.

majorStructure.text: Business, engineering, music and dance have direct-entry review. Sociology, History and Anthropology list no separate application, course, credit or GPA threshold to declare after university admission.

recommendedMajors.text: Sociology, History and Anthropology are options for academic exploration. Their open declaration rules are not lower freshman admission thresholds.

ap.text: AP may earn credit under the exam-specific Guide table. Send official College Board results; AP exams must be completed in high school. Credit is not an admission guarantee.

cost.text: Tuition depends on program, credits and residency; the Bursar publishes the2026–27 rate workbook. A complete current international annual budget was not verified here. Request tuition, housing, insurance and travel totals before shortlisting.

aid.text: International applicants can search WiSH scholarships. F/J international students do not qualify for federal or Wisconsin state aid. Scholarship deadlines are often February1 or earlier; confirm2028 and any CSS requirement with Financial Aid.

admission.text: Holistic review; Ohio State states no minimum GPA, class rank or SAT/ACT score. This does not mean low grades are competitive.

acceptanceRate.text: No defined-cohort acceptance percentage is used.

sat.text: ACT or SAT is required for first-year Columbus applicants in the current Autumn2027 instructions. Official scores and superscoring are used; confirm Fall2028.

satMiddle50.text: The current admissions page shows1280–1470 for the admitted-student SAT middle50%, but does not identify the year. It is retained as an undated reference, not used as a dated comparison cohort.

satTarget.text: No Ontario-grade×SAT formula is published.1100–1500 scenarios cannot establish admission from a score alone.

deadlines.text: Fall2028 deadlines are not yet verified. Autumn2027: EA November1,2026; RD January15,2027; acceptance fee May1,2027. All required materials must arrive by the application deadline.

application.text: Common App; international fee USD70. Official Grades9–12 records and testing; recommendations optional (maximum two).

ontario.text: Send original official records for the final four secondary years. No Ontario top-six formula or percentage minimum is published in the reviewed guidance.

coursework.text: University-preparatory coursework, rigor and achievement are reviewed. Ask Admissions to confirm Ontario U/M equivalencies for the intended program.

international.text: International classification excludes U.S. citizens, permanent residents, refugees and asylees. International applicants must choose a degree major; undecided/University Exploration is unavailable.

english.text: Examples: IELTS6.5, DET120, SAT reading/writing550; TOEFL4.0 from January21,2026. Canadian citizenship outside Quebec is listed among exemptions; Ontario attendance alone is not that exemption. Confirm individual status.

majorStructure.text: Admission is reviewed first, then enrollment in the intended college/major. Humanities generally admit directly; some other fields start as competitive pre-majors. This is not proof of easier university admission.

recommendedMajors.text: History and Ancient History/Classics permit declaration upon university admission. Sociology is available as BA/BS; its curriculum lists Sociology1101 before declaration. No first-year Ontario cutoff is stated for these majors.

ap.text: AP3+ earns credit under the subject table. Psychology3+ gives PSYCH1100; Statistics3 gives STAT1450,4+ gives STAT2450. Send College Board scores; the entry-term policy controls awards.

cost.text: 2026–27 international annual components: tuition/fees USD47,374; housing/food15,630; books1,020; insurance4,108; personal4,046. Listed components total USD72,178; travel and individual costs can add more. Not2028 prices.

aid.text: International students are excluded from the university-funded first-year merit awards listed on the admissions page and must demonstrate funds for tuition/living costs. Confirm external/departmental options and2028 CSS needs directly.

admission.text: Purdue evaluates preparation and competition within the chosen major. It does not offer one admission formula; campus and program capacity matter.

acceptanceRate.text: The2026 class-profile page reports53.3% overall for West Lafayette+Indianapolis together. This combined rate is not an Ontario, international or specific-major probability.

sat.text: Purdue expects SAT, ACT or CLT scores; applications without testing are allowed in exceptional cases. The2026 guide says98.3% of admitted students provided a test score. Recheck Fall2028.

satMiddle50.text: Fall2026 published SAT middle50%: overall1230–1480, Liberal Arts1110–1348, Education1040–1208, Engineering1390–1520. The page covers West Lafayette+Indianapolis together; college figures are not major-specific minimums.

satTarget.text: Compare your score with the intended college, not only the university aggregate. A lower college distribution does not guarantee entry, particularly with weak school grades.

deadlines.text: Fall2028 dates are not verified. Current reference: November1 EA for priority majors, Honors and merit consideration; fall applications close January15. Recheck program availability.

application.text: Common App essay, Purdue responses, self-reported grades and testing, fee or eligible waiver. Choose campus and major; an alternate is allowed. Current international undergraduate fee amount was not verified here.

ontario.text: Submit Grades9–11 while in school; graduates submit Grades9–12 and OSSD. Purdue encourages at least six4U/4M courses to be competitive. No Ontario percentage minimum is given.

coursework.text: Published Sociology minimum preparation: English4 years, math4, lab science3, social studies3, world language2. International curriculum exceptions may apply; confirm Ontario equivalents.

international.text: International curriculum records and English requirements apply as relevant; some citizenship categories have additional review. Confirm status-specific instructions rather than treating Ontario attendance as citizenship.

english.text: Current guidance: IELTS6.5 with each6.0; DET115 with each110; TOEFL4.5 with each4.0 for tests from January21,2026. SAT reading/writing600 is accepted. Three English-medium years with B-equivalent English grades and strong academics may be considered.

majorStructure.text: Apply directly to a major and location. Sociology/History are West Lafayette Liberal Arts; Elementary Education is in Education. A later change of major or campus is never guaranteed.

recommendedMajors.text: Explore Sociology, History or Elementary Education only for genuine interest. Education has its own teaching preparation and licensing pathway. College-level SAT differences are evidence for comparing cohorts, not a lowest-entry major ranking.

ap.text: AP Psychology4/5 maps to PSY12000; Statistics4/5 to STAT30100; English Language4/5 to ENGL10600. Scores3 may yield undistributed credit. Send official scores and recheck2028 equivalencies.

cost.text: 2026–27 full-time annual international tuition components shown: general service USD9,718, nonresident18,802, international3,310, fitness234, activity40, differential general service1,800. Housing, food and other expenses are additional; specialized programs add differentials. Not2028 prices.

aid.text: The Purdue Common App page restricts its full range of freshman merit scholarships to U.S. citizens/permanent residents. Do not assume a Canadian applicant qualifies. Confirm any separate international awards and CSS/need-based process directly.
